### ① Derived judgments

**Check-runs on `9e0ae37b`, read three times until none was open.** At 2026-10-26T16:24Z: 48 runs, 7 in progress. At 2026-10-26T16:27Z: 50 runs, 1 in progress. At 2026-10-26T16:30:47Z: 51 runs, 34 success, 17 skipped, 0 in progress, 0 failure. The gate-carrying ones: `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success at 2026-10-26T16:21:15Z (its first step runs the head's own `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --self-test` under `bash -e`, so a red predicate reds the check; its live step is the `pull_request` early-warning leg, exit 0 on this governed draft); `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests` success at 2026-10-26T16:22:46Z (`check-self-test-workflow-commands.mjs` spawns every CI-run script that ships a `--self-test`, both governed scripts among them); `Lint · repo & tooling gates` success at 2026-10-26T16:24:55Z (lint.yml lines 1041, 1051, 1538, 1559: `check:pm-skill-ratchet`, `check:pm-skill-id-lint`, `check:pm-governed-merges` which IS the sibling's `--self-test`, `check:pm-governed-prose`); `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` success at 2026-10-26T16:26:05Z; `Lint · ESLint` success at 2026-10-26T16:23:45Z; `Lint · docs & code guards` success at 2026-10-26T16:25:00Z; `Check Changeset` success.

**Every rule the diff adds, removes or narrows, judged against the order, the triage boundary and the guard's regime:**

1. ADDS the enqueue limb to `entrySatisfied`: `approval.state === 'approved'` first, then `enqueue.state === 'authorized'`, then the Tier S record — RIGHT. The order is 「大部分我还是希望入队，但是我想省掉 Approve」 with the logins 「os-zhuang 或 hotlong」; `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` is `Object.freeze(['os-zhuang', 'hotlong'])` on `origin/main` (line 621) and on the head (line 689), unchanged, and the limb reads it through `GOVERNED_APPROVERS.includes`, never a copy. Only the `merge_group` leg consults it: `runGuard` reads the timeline under `event === EVENT_MERGE_GROUP` alone, and `guardVerdict` attaches the `enqueue` key on that event alone. An enqueue by any other account is `unauthorized` and the entry still needs the review.
2. ADDS `enqueuerFromTimeline`, `authorizedEnqueueVerdict`, `undeterminedEnqueue` (pure) and `makeTimelineReader` (paged `GET /repos/{slug}/issues/{n}/timeline`) — RIGHT; traced under (a).
3. ADDS the same predicate to the SIZE limb through the sibling: `sizeLiftFrom` reads the approval lift first, then `enqueue.state === 'authorized'` with a non-empty login; `unauthorized` and `undetermined` lift nothing; `renderLiftApprovals` prints the enqueuer — RIGHT against card §4 and the claim amendment. `check-governed-merges.mjs` moved in exactly four hunks: the new `SIZE_ENQUEUE_LIFT_RULING` constant (the citation string `sizeLiftFrom` returns, beside `SIZE_LIFT_RULING`), `sizeLiftFrom`, `renderLiftApprovals`, and three self-test pins; the `authorizedVerdict` helper already took `extra` on `origin/main` (line 6393). Nothing else in the file moved.
4. NARROWS nothing. The `pull_request` leg, the 2026-09-04 approval predicate, the Tier S record leg, the fork rule, `GOVERNED_APPROVERS`, `.github/CODEOWNERS` and `governed-surface-guard.yml` are unchanged (`git diff origin/main 9e0ae37b` on the workflow and CODEOWNERS is empty).
5. CHANGES the rendering only where card §3 asks: the enqueue-leg line names the leg and the account, a third CLEARED wording never claims an approval it did not read, and a refusal names `unauthorized` or `UNDETERMINED` with the reason — RIGHT.
6. AGENTS.md: three edits, judged under (d).

**(a) Fail-closed — the code on the head, not the body.** `runGuard` reads the approval first and reaches the timeline only when `approvals.get(pr)?.state !== 'approved'`; an unreadable review list reaches it too, because an authorized enqueue is a record of its own, as an approval is. Fixture 3 pins that an authorized approval never reads the timeline (`apiCalls === 2`). UNDETERMINED never passes: `entrySatisfied` passes on the literal `'authorized'` and nothing else; `undeterminedEnqueue` is the value for no reader, a throw (non-2xx, non-array body, truncation), no add event, an actorless add, and a newest queue event that is a removal; `entryUnreadable` is untouched and reads only `approval.state === 'unreadable'` and the Tier S record, so the exit code stays today's — 3 with no review (fixture 4), 4 with an unreadable review list beside a seat enqueue (pinned). Unauthorized never passes (fixture 2: exit 3 with today's words "NO authorized APPROVED review on this pull request" plus the new reason line). A verdict built with no `enqueues` entry for a non-approved queue entry is filled with `undeterminedEnqueue`, never a default pass. The loop has no `continue` that skips both readings: a `fetchPull` throw is a head note only, a `fetchReviews` throw lands in `unreadableApproval`, and the enqueue block runs after either.

Stale adds and ordering: `enqueuerFromTimeline` keeps the LAST add-or-remove event in array order; a removal newest is UNDETERMINED, so an earlier authorized add is never carried onto a re-entry whose add is not yet recorded; a re-queue after an ejection reads its own actor, so a seat's re-enqueue is `unauthorized` and needs the approval or another click. Measured on #26011: three add/remove cycles, every removal recorded with actor `github-merge-queue[bot]`, every add attributed to the arming account and never to the queue bot, so the "enqueued by GitHub's own actor" shape does not occur on this repository — and if it ever did, the queue bot's login is outside the constant and refuses. A merge group carrying several PRs is judged per `entry.pr`, each with its own timeline read, so one authorized enqueue carries no sibling; the existing `partial` approval case pins that loop shape and there is no enqueue-specific mixed-group case (non-blocking gap).

Attribution of an auto-merge-armed entry, re-measured. The body's fleet cases hold: #26154 `auto_merge_enabled` actor `objectstack-fleet[bot]` at 2026-10-26T14:44:16Z, `added_to_merge_queue` actor `objectstack-fleet[bot]` at 2026-10-26T14:46:53Z. The case the body left unmeasured — a HUMAN arming — I measured on eight Tier H landings: armed then enqueued, `auto_merge_enabled` actor `os-zhuang` then `added_to_merge_queue` actor `os-zhuang` (#26017 at 2026-10-26T09:20:48Z then 2026-10-26T09:23:25Z; #25969; #25930); direct enqueue with no `auto_merge_enabled` event and add actor `os-zhuang` (#26097, #26058, #25971, #25816, #25717). `merged_by` read `os-zhuang` on all eight: on a queue landing `merged_by` IS the enqueuer, which is the column the post-merge audit lists. `auto_merge` is null on every merged PR read, so the body is right not to read `enabled_by`.

Paging: `per_page=100`, pages 1 to 10, returns on the first short page, throws past 1,000 events. The timeline is oldest-first on every read above (ascending `created_at`), so the newest event is on the last page and the walk reaches it; a cut walk throws and the caller turns it into UNDETERMINED. Pinned by the two-page walk, the truncation throw and the HTTP 403 throw. Token scope: the route answers `X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions: issues=read; pull_requests=read` on four timelines I read; the workflow holds `contents: read` and `pull-requests: read` and is untouched. Unmeasured by anyone: the `merge_group` job's own `GITHUB_TOKEN` making that read; if refused, the leg prints `enqueuer UNDETERMINED — the timeline could not be read (HTTP 403)` and the approval leg decides, which is today's behaviour, loud, never a pass. Non-blocking: array order is trusted over `created_at` (the header says so); the API is chronological and the pure function is pinned on that order.

**(b) Identity floor.** PD14 already carries "before that record no AI seat merges, queues, or arms auto-merge" and "⛔ never queue, ⛔ never arm auto-merge"; the new sentence 「An authorized account's enqueue is a review record too: ⛔ never a seat's.」 sits directly after the approving-review prohibition ("under any account — an authorized account is agent-operated too") and inherits "under any account" by construction, so the floor is stated where the rule lives. The guard header states it in the approval side's own words and names the exposure honestly: the prohibition "is the ONLY thing between an agent seat holding an authorized account and a governed landing it cleared for itself". On #11704: the new section quotes the founding ruling (`check-governed-merges.mjs` line 330, verbatim 「人工合并即人工审核:governed PR 的审核记录 = 你按下合并/入队那个动作本身」) and rests the leg on the normative floor; the material difference — a push is authorship, open to every seat, while the enqueue click is a deliberate, timestamped act on the PR that PD14 reserves exactly as it reserves the approval — is said in substance. FLAG, prose only: the older bound at header lines 120-123 of the head ("attribution from the GitHub actor field is not a reading … never on who pushed or merged") survives unamended and now reads as contradicted by the new section; by the header's own convention the dated later layer governs, but that sentence should be marked superseded-in-part the way the 2026-09-04 section marks the sha-pin half. Same class as the stale "pinned to the current head" bullet the dev reported out of scope.

**(c) Scope kept.** PR leg: no timeline read, no `enqueue` key, output free of the line by construction (pinned). Tier S: unchanged except that the enqueue limb sits between approval and record, so a Tier S entry the maintainer enqueued clears without a record read — the symmetric case of an authorized approval, which already cleared it. `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` unchanged; CODEOWNERS and `codeownersMirrorVerdict` unchanged, self-test green twice. Size lift: the enqueue lift is read after the approval lift and nothing wider; an `unreadable` review list beside an authorized enqueue lifts exactly as the governed leg passes it, and a seat enqueue on an oversized PR still exits 8 (pinned). The sibling touched only as the amendment allows. No widening found.

**(d) AGENTS.md.** 1,117 lines on `origin/main` and on the head (measured); the six changed lines are 118, 118, 118, 118, 113 and 38 bytes under `MAX_LINE_BYTES = 120`; the widest row (a table row, structurally exempt) is 768 bytes on both; the ceiling row `['AGENTS.md', 1117]` is unmoved. The three edits say the guard's rule: line 264 "Tier H by the maintainer's hand (merge or enqueue) or an authorized approval"; line 290 the new sentence; §7 (c) lines 519-520 "or the maintainer's merge or enqueue" for "or a human merge". Nothing the old sentences carried is lost: the register enumeration, the Tier S clause, the fork clause and the `get_files` / author / size reading all survive, and no date, number or quotation entered a rule line. The ratchet's job, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, is green on the head; so is `check:pm-governed-prose` in the same job.

**(e) Self-test and ablation.** The battery `⭐ the 2026-10-26 ENQUEUE leg` pins 28 and I count 28 assertions in the hunk; the roster floor moves 27 to 28 with its row. It pins what (a) requires — the four card fixtures, the stale add (pure, and through `runGuard` on exit 3), no reader, truncation, non-2xx — and beyond them: an unreadable review list beside an authorized enqueue (0) and a seat enqueue (4), the API-call count, the PR leg reading nothing, a clear diff reading nothing, Tier S clearing without a record read, approval-first, the oversized lift (0) and its refusal (8), one timeline read across both limbs, `main()`'s wiring read from its own source, and the paged walk. The sibling's three pins cover the authorized lift, no-lift on unauthorized / undetermined / empty login, and approval-first. Verdicts on the head: the guard's self-test green in `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and in the tooling self-tests lane; the sibling's green in `Lint · repo & tooling gates`. The body's 373 / 537 counts and the two ablations (5 and 1 red, restored, blob equal to HEAD) are the dev's report, consistent with the diff, not re-run here.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right: the three paths are `scripts/pm/**` and `AGENTS.md`, and neither ships in a released package; `Check Changeset` success on the head. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` stand line-initial after `Fixes #26066` (the relay's two attribution lines precede it) and are right: no spec, export or authorable key moves.

- Body "Not measured" ②, an entry armed from an authorized account reaching the queue: CLOSED by this review's reading of #26017, #25969 and #25930 (armed) and five direct ones — the add actor is the human.
- Open question A / B (`pnpm lint`, `check:governed-queue-guard-self-test`): A stands. `package.json` has no such script (verified; `check:pm-governed-merges` and `check:pm-governed-prose` exist, the guard's self-test is a derived family and ran in CI), and `Lint · ESLint` ran the repo-wide lint on the head. os-dev.md wins the conflict, as the order itself says.

- Accepted cost, for the maintainer's eye and already stated in the header and the 维护者速读 ②: a push after the click and before the entry lands is not re-reviewed, the 2026-09-04 shape. It is real on this repository: #26138 was armed from `os-zhuang` at 2026-10-26T14:14:54Z while red, and seat commits followed for two hours; under the new leg those would land under the click, as they already would under his approval.
